observations.contents: E7D5: Slack-branded card (header '# Slack'). Title 'このメッセージを送りますか？' (Send this message?). Below title, an orange flagged line '↗ 外部に出る' (going external). Labeled fields: 宛先 (To) = #sales, 差出人 (From) = あなた (You). Full message body shown in Japanese ('明日の会議、資料を先に共有します。10月の導入時期の件も入れておきました。'), not truncated. A provenance/source line '出所 週次同期・田中・10:42 >' (expandable). Buttons: Cancel (text), Edit (blue text link), 送る/Send (filled orange button, primary). | 91C2: Gmail-branded card (Gmail logo + 'Gmail' label, X close icon top-right). Title 'Send this message?'. Labeled fields: To = hello@voiceos.com, Subject = Meeting tomorrow. 'Message Preview:' shows a truncated snippet ending in an ellipsis ('Hey team, just wanted to follow up on our meeting tomorrow…'), not the full message. No provenance/source field. Buttons: Send (filled blue, primary), Edit (outlined secondary button); an X icon also serves as an implicit cancel/close.
observations.sizes: As captured, E7D5's PNG is 560x229px (~128k px²) and 91C2's is 500x200px (~100k px²), so E7D5's crop is roughly 25-30% larger in raw area. However these are screenshot crops, not confirmed to be at the same on-screen scale/DPI, so true relative on-screen footprint cannot be reliably compared — noting E7D5 also carries one extra line of information (the external-flag warning and provenance line) that 91C2 does not have, which partly explains the larger crop.

why.action_clarity: Both lead with a bold, unambiguous 'send this?' question above the same core fields, so speed-to-understanding is equivalent.
why.parameter_hierarchy: E7D5 labels recipient/sender AND surfaces an explicit external-destination flag ('外部に出る'), giving the decisive channel/audience info more prominence than 91C2's plain To/Subject labels.
why.preview_readability: E7D5 shows the complete message text, while 91C2's 'Message Preview' is truncated with an ellipsis, so you cannot fully verify what will actually be sent.
why.control_visibility: Both surface three controls (E7D5: Cancel/Edit/Send; 91C2: Send/Edit/X-close) with a clear primary action, but each has one weaker element (E7D5's Edit is a small text link; 91C2's cancel is only an unlabeled X), so neither is clearly better.
why.screen_occupation: 91C2 delivers the same confirm/edit/send job in a visually smaller, more compact card despite carrying slightly less information.
why.visual_craft: 91C2's rounded card, generous padding, and centered icon/button treatment read as more polished and spacious; E7D5 is denser and more utilitarian in its spacing.
why.error_prevention: E7D5's explicit 'going external' warning plus a provenance line lets the user catch a wrong-audience or wrong-source send before approving, which 91C2 has no equivalent for.
why.provenance_visibility: E7D5 has a dedicated, expandable source line ('出所 週次同期・田中・10:42'); 91C2 shows no origin/source information at all.
